title: tb-scaffold.json contract (post-materialize)
description: Structural contract for <module>/Verification/simulation-plan/tb-scaffold.json, validated by the check-scaffold gate AFTER the materialize-scaffold verb has run. The sequence roster and the power scenarios live in their own files (sequences.json / power-scenarios.json); what remains here is what simulation alone reads. Every field below says whether it is yours to author or script-injected, and carries the authoring judgment no validator can express. Every field here is the plan author's judgment. What the DUT looks like is NOT restated: simulation reads top-io.json and clocks.json directly at render time, so the signals, the clocks and the reset polarity cannot drift from what specification declared, and cannot be partial — a port missing from a copy rendered as a DUT port bound to nothing, which Verilog accepts and VCS compiles without an error. Referential integrity (observer/inports/seqs resolving to declared agents, and sequences.json/power-scenarios.json resolving against each other) is NOT expressible here; the check-scaffold gate's semantic layer enforces it.

mode.description: `active` for a driver/master group you drive, `passive` for a monitor/slave group you only observe. Take it from the group's top-io.json `direction` values.

interface_groups.description: top-io.json `interface_group` names. Ports sharing a group become one virtual interface and this one agent.

test_id.description: Stable per-test identifier; the regression log keys results by it.

suites.description: Which suites run this test — `["smoke", "regress"]` or `["regress"]`. YOUR judgment as the plan author, not a script's: `make smoke` is the fast pre-check, `make regress` runs everything. A smoke test is one whose failure means the design is broken badly enough that running the rest is pointless — the datapath itself, or the register path every other test loads its stimulus through. Pick them by that, not by position in the list; most modules need two or three.

inports.description: The agents[].name values whose monitor streams feed the RM — one analysis_imp port each. YOUR judgment: which agents feed the reference model. Name the AGENT, not its transaction type: simulation's renderer builds the type as <module>_<agent>_txn where it needs one, so a name written here in txn form would have to be un-wrapped and re-wrapped to reach the same string. The gate only checks the names resolve.

observer.description: The ONE agents[].name whose monitor stream the scoreboard compares against the RM. Omitted only when a single agent is declared; with more than one, omitting it is ambiguous and the gate rejects it.

intent.description: What this testpoint drives and why — the situation being created, not the check (the covered hints already say how each check is verified). It is the whole of what a reader has: simulation's verify child judges against it whether an uncovered branch or FSM transition falls inside this testpoint's remit, and an item it cannot place is routed back here as a missing testpoint.

covers.description: The `check-hints/<child>.json` check_ids this testpoint verifies — YOUR clustering (one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-one). Present with an explicit empty array on a scenario testpoint you invented, since omitted and `[]` are not the same claim; an empty one verifies no authored check. Simulation reads each covered hint, and the requirements.json rows it names, by id.

seqs.description: The sequences[] names whose stimulus is meant to drive this testpoint. YOUR judgment: `tests[].seqs` says what a testcase runs, this says which of those the testpoint rides on. simulation's verify child reads it when classifying an uncovered item — it places an uncovered branch on a testpoint and this is what tells it whose stimulus to iterate. A testpoint no sequence drives cannot be exercised, so name at least one.

skipped_checks.description: Every check_hints[] check_id no testpoint covers, each with why. The coverage-matrix gate accepts a check_id only as covered or skipped, so this is where a check that has no runtime testpoint is accounted for.

reason.description: Why no testpoint verifies it, e.g. "static lint gate, no runtime testpoint".
